QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_13

question.text: Mandakini Buyout Fund has called 100% of its INR 800 crore committed capital (PIC = commitment). Cumulative distributions are INR 600 crore and residual NAV is INR 900 crore. What are MOIC and TVPI, respectively?

answer.text: MOIC = 1.875, TVPI = 1.125 (they differ because commitments > PIC)
MOIC = 1.875, TVPI = 1.875 (equal because all capital called)

explanation.text: The Logic: MOIC = (Realised + Unrealised Value) / Total Invested Capital = (600+900)/800 = 1500/800 = 1.875. TVPI = (Distributions + Residual Value) / PIC = (600+900)/800 = 1.875. Per Section 7.3.4.4: 'when all the capital calls are met, total invested capital equals total paid-in capital; thereby TVPI equals MOIC.' The Trap: A manufactures a difference that doesn't exist when PIC = Commitment. B uses incorrect denominators. C inverts the ratio. Note: When PIC < Commitment (dry powder remains), MOIC and TVPI can diverge because MOIC uses invested capital as the denominator while TVPI uses paid-in capital.
